title: Rama and Lakshmana travel with Vishvamitra
introduction: King Dasharatha sends Rama and Lakshmana along with Sage Vishvamitra as requested by the sage. In their course of travel, Sage Vishvamitra imparts a secret knowledge to the young princes Rama and Lakshmana, called bala-atibala- vidya-s, by practicing which nothing can wither their vigour and vitality.
closing: balātibalayoḥ virāṭpuruṣaḥ ṛṣiḥ | gāyatrī devatā | gāyatrī candaḥ | akārokāramakārā bījādyāḥ | kṣudhādi nirasane viniyogaḥ | klāmityādi ṣaḍañganyāsaḥ | klām añguṣṭābhyām namaḥ | klīm tarjanībhyām namaḥ | klūm madhyamābhyām namaḥ | klaim anāmikābhyām namaḥ | klom kaniṣṭikābhyām namaḥ | klaḥ karatalakarapṛṣṭābhyām namaḥ || klām hṛdayāya namaḥ | klīm śirase svāhā | klūm śikhāyai vaṣaṭ | klaim kavacāya hum | klom netratrayāya vauṣaṭ | klaḥ astrāya phaṭ | bhūrbhūvassuvaromiti digbandhaḥ |
amṛtakaratalādau sarvasañjīvanāḍhyā avaghaharaṇa sudkṣau vedasāre mayūkhe | praṇavamayavikārau bhāskarākāradehau satatamanubhave'ham tau balātibaleṣu ||

om hrīm bale mahādevi hrīm mahābale klīm caturvidhapuruṣārthasiddhiprade tatsaviturvaradātmike hrīm vareṇyam bhargo devasya varadātmike | atibale sarvadayāmūrte bale sarvakṣudbhramopanāśini dhīmahi dhiyoyonarjāte pracuryā pracodayātmike praṇavaśiraskātmike | hum phaṭ svāhā || evam vidvān kṛtakṛtyo bhavati | sāvitryā eva salokatām jayati || ityupaniṣat ||

om āpyāyantu mamāñgāni vākprāṇaścakṣuḥ śrotramatho balamindriyāṇi ca sarvāṇi | sarvam brahmopaniṣadam | māham brahma nirākuryām mā mā brahma nirākarot | anirākaraṇamastu anirākaraṇam me'stuḥ tadātmani nirate ye upaniṣatsu dharmāste mayi santu te mayi santu || om śāntiśśāntiśśāntiḥ |

Sage Vishvamitra is the Seer for Gayatri hymn. He is the same Sage to impart balaatibala hymns to Rama and Lakshmana. For those readers that are interested to know or to practice, the Upanishad of balaatibala is included hereunder. This hymn is yet another aspect of Gayatri, and there is no hymn superior than Gayatri, na gaayatryaaH paramam japam
इति वाल्मीकिरामायणे आदिकाव्ये बालकाण्डे द्वाविंशः सर्गः ||
Thus, this is the 22nd chapter in Bala Kanda of Valmiki Ramayana, the First Epic poem of India.

verses.devanagari:
तथा वसिष्ठे ब्रुवति राजा दशरथः स्वयम् |
प्रहृष्टवदनो राममाजुहाव सलक्ष्मणम्
verses.iast:
tathā vasiṣṭe bruvati rājā daśarathaḥ svayam |
prahṛṣṭa vadano rāmam ājuhāva sa lakṣmaṇam
verses.translation: When Vashishta said that way king Dasharatha with an air of satisfaction personally fetched Rama along with Lakshmana.

glosses.meaning: by Vashishta, that way, when said
Rama, with Lakshmana, is called for.

verses.devanagari:
कृतस्वस्त्ययनं मात्रा पित्रा दशरथेन च |
पुरोधसा वसिष्ठेन मङ्गलैरभिमंत्रितम्
सपुत्रं मूर्ध्न्युपाघ्राय राजा दशरथस्तदा |
ददौ कुशिकपुत्राय सुप्रीतेनान्तरात्मना
verses.iast:
kṛtaḥ svastyayanam mātrā pitrā daśarathena ca |
purodhasā vasiṣṭhena mañgalaiḥ abhimantritam
sa putram mūrdhni upāghrāya rājā daśarathaḥ tadā |
dadau kuśika putrāya suprītena antarātmanā
verses.translation: Rama is blessed for a propitious travel firstly by his mother Kausalya and then by his father king Dasharatha, thereupon the royal priest Vashishta rendered Vedic hymns blessing the journey, then Dasharatha well pleased in his heart of hearts kissed his son Rama on forehead and entrusted him to Vishvamitra.
notes: The mother is the first one to bless sons. prathamam mātṛ kṛta mañgala pratipadanena itara kṛta mañgala apekṣayā mātṛ kṛta mañgalasya āvaśyikatā vyatirekeṇa anvayena ca sūcitam

Duryodhana of Maha Bharata knows about this rule position and when he wanted to gain victory over Pandava-s he approaches his mother Gandhari, seeking her blessings, at first. vyatirekaḥ tāvat pāṇḍavān jetu kāmo duryodhanaḥ - śivam āśamsa me mātaḥ yudhyamāna sva śatrubhiḥ - iti aṣṭā daśa āhāni ap sva mātaram gāndhārīm prārthitavān | sa ca - yato dharmaḥ tato jayaḥ - iti vadantī mañgalam na kurvatī - dharmākūtam When Duryodhana sought for his mother Gandhari's blessings even for eighteen days, where eighteen is the particular number of Maha Bharata, she said 'where there is virtue there will be victory'. Hence, mothers are the first ones to bless sons in every enterprise, and here Rama's enterprise as incarnate of Vishnu is commencing.

glosses.meaning: one [for whom bon voyage is] performed, blessing, for travel - Rama
blessings, [for who they are] rendered Vedic hymns
well, pleased, with heart of hearts

verses.devanagari:
ततो वायुः सुखस्पर्शो नीरजस्को ववौ तदा |
विश्वामित्रगतं रामं दृष्ट्वा राजीवलोचनम्
verses.iast:
tato vāyuḥ sukha sparśo nīrajasko vavau tadā |
viśvāmitra gatam rāmam dṛṣṭvā rājīva locanam
verses.translation: Then on seeing the lotus-eyed Rama following Vishvamitra the breeze became dustless and breezed pleasant for touch.

verses.iast:
puṣpa vṛṣṭiḥ mahatI āsīt deva dundubhi niḥsvanaiḥ |
śañkha dundubhi nirghoṣaḥ prayāte tu mahātmani
verses.translation: When the great-souled Rama forged ahead there occurred an abounding downpour of flowers with the booming of divine drums, together with the boom and blare of drums and conch-shells of Ayodhya.

verses.devanagari:
विश्वामित्रो ययावग्रे ततो रामो महायशाः |
काकपक्षधरो धन्वी तं च सौमित्रिरन्वगात्
verses.iast:
viśvāmitro yayau agre tato rāmo mahāyaśāḥ |
kāka pakṣa dharo dhanvī tam ca saumitriḥ anvagāt
verses.translation: Rama with jet-black hair-locks handling his bow followed Vishvamitra who walked ahead, while Lakshmana handling his own bow followed Rama.

verses.devanagari:
कलापिनौ धनुष्पाणी शोभयानौ दिशो दश |
विश्वामित्रं महात्मानं त्रिशीर्षाविव पन्नगौ |
अनुजग्मतुरक्षुद्रौ पितामहमिवाश्विनौ
verses.iast:
kalāpinau dhanuṣ pāṇī śobhayānau diśo daśa |
viśvāmitram mahātmānam tri śīrṣau iva pannagau |
anujagmatuḥ akṣudrau pitāmaham iva aśvinau
verses.translation: Rama and Lakshmana, with two quivers each and two bows in their hands, and making all the ten directions of compass lambent followed Vishvamitra, as if three headed serpents followed Vishvamitra, and with their highly dynamic physiques and spiritedness they look as if like the Ashwin twin gods of unequal charm following Brahma, the Forefather.
notes: Each one is having two quivers tied on each shoulder. Thus the upper portions of the quivers with feathered shafts, with the tips of arrows inside, are giving a picture of two more heads, on either side of the princes' heads. Thus Rama and Lakshmana are appearing like three headed serpents. That is to say they are too young with the size of their heads equalling the mouth of the quiver.

The meaning of As'vins from as'va a horse, Persian asp, Greek ιππος Latin equus, Welsh *eck, is Horsemen. They were twin deities of whom frequent mention is made in the Vedas and the Indian myths. The As'vins have much in common with the Dioscuri of Greece, and their mythical genealogy seems to indicate that their origin was astronomical. They were, perhaps, at first the morning star and evening star. They are said to be the children of the sun and the nymph As'vin, who is one of the lunar asterisms personified. In the popular mythology they are regarded as the physicians of the Gods. Gorresio/Griffith.

glosses.itrans: a kshudrau analpa ruupa viiryaadi prabhaavaaH
glosses.iast: a kśudrau analpa rūpa vīryādi prabhāvāḥ
glosses.devanagari: अ क्शुद्रौ अनल्प रूप वीर्यादि प्रभावाः
glosses.meaning: not, with meagre physical and vital impact =- highly dynamic in physiques and spiritedness
the twin Ashwin gods, after Forefather Brahma, as with

verses.devanagari:
तदा कुशिकपुत्रं तु धनुष्पाणी स्वलंकृतौ |
बद्धगोधांगुलित्राणौ खड्गवन्तौ महाद्युती
कुमारौ चारुवपुषौ भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ |
अनुयातौ श्रिया दीप्तौ शोभयेतामनिन्दितौ
स्थाणुं देवमिवाचिन्त्यं कुमाराविव पावकी |
verses.iast:
tadā kuśika putram tu dhanuṣ pāṇī svalaṅkṛtau |
baddha godha aṅguli trāṇau khaḍgavantau mahādyutī
kumārau cāru vapuṣau bhrātarau rāma laxmaṇau |
anuyātau śriyā dIptau śobhayetām aninditau
sthāṇum devam iva acintyam kumārau iva pāvakī |
verses.translation: Those two youngsters with charming and bejewelled physiques are handling bows and swords and their fingers have leathern covers. Both the unreprovable brothers Rama and Lakshmana are highly resplendent and effulgent by their worth. While they are following Vishvamitra they looked like the sons of Fire-god, namely Skanda and Vishakha, following the great god with inscrutable potential, namely Shiva, and thus the brothers have made Vishvamitra to shine forth in even pose with god Shiva.
notes: The Supreme Being that is resident like an atom. stha Being, aṇum atom like. In every mobile or sessile being he is there. Here it is Shiva. Shiva's sons are two, one Ganesha and the other Kumara, of which Kumara is the Army General of Gods. According to Maha Bharata, Kumara is said to have become four in a split-second, known as 1- Skanda, 2- Vishaakha, 3- Shaaka, 4- Naigamesha. Here the first two aspects of Kumara, namely Skanda and Vishaakha, are incorporated in simile to Rama and Lakshmana.

glosses.meaning: not, thinkable - inscrutable potential, the god - Shiva

verses.devanagari:
अध्यर्धयोजनं गत्वा सरय्वा दक्षिणे तटे |
रामेति मधुरां वाणीं विश्वामित्रोऽभ्यभाषत |
verses.iast:
adhyardha yojanam gatvā sarayvā dakṣiṇe taṭe |
rāmā iti madhurām vāṇīm viśvāmitraḥ abhyabhāṣata |
verses.translation: And on going one and half yojana distance Vishvamitra addressed Rama in a harmonious voice calling, 'oh, Rama', on the southern riverbank of Sarayu.

glosses.meaning: one and half, yojana on going

verses.devanagari:
गृहाण वत्स सलिलं मा भूत् कालस्य पर्ययः
मंत्रग्रामं गृहाण त्वं बलामतिबलां तथा |
verses.iast:
gṛhāṇa vatsa salilam mā bhūt kālasya paryayaḥ
mantra grāmam gṛhāṇa tvam balām atibalām tathā |
verses.translation: " "Take water, my boy, and like that you receive a group of hymns, bala and ati bala from me, and let no time lapse.
notes: Since the Vedic hymns cannot be taught after sunset, now it shall be evening time before sunset, when oblations will be offered at sunset, and hence no time lapse is envisaged. Govindaraja.

glosses.meaning: time's, lapse , not, let there be.

verses.devanagari:
न श्रमो न ज्वरो वा ते न रूपस्य विपर्ययः
न च सुप्तं प्रमत्तं वा धर्षयिष्यन्ति नैरृताः |
verses.iast:
na śramo na jvaro vā te na rūpasya viparyayaḥ
na ca suptam pramattam vā dharṣa iṣyanti nairṛtāḥ |
verses.translation: "On receiving these hymns neither tiredness nor fever, nor disfiguring of personality can effect you, nor the demons can charge you either you are sleeping or unvigilant.

verses.devanagari:
न बाह्वोः सदृशो वीर्ये पृथिव्यामस्ति कश्चन
त्रिषु लोकेषु वा राम न भवेत्सदृशस्तव |
verses.iast:
na bāhvoḥ sadṛśo vīrye pṛthivyām asti kaścana
triṣu lokeṣu vā rāma na bhavet sadṛśaḥ tava |
verses.translation: "As it is none whosoever on earth can equal you in dexterity, Rama, and by reciting these hymns none can equal you in the three worlds.

verses.devanagari:
बलामतिबलां चैव पठतस्तात राघव
न सौभाग्ये न दाक्षिण्ये न ज्ञाने बुद्धिनिश्चये |
नोत्तरे प्रतिवक्तव्ये समो लोके तवानघ
verses.iast:
balām atibalām caiva paṭhataḥ tāta rāghava
na saubhāgye na dākṣiṇye na GYāne buddhi niścaye |
na uttare prati vaktavye samo loke tava anagha
verses.translation: "My dear Raghava, if bala atibala hymns are practised, oh, impeccable one, none can equal you in the world by your handsomeness, calibre, erudition, by your discernment, and even in replying or rebutting you.

glosses.meaning: in handsomeness [apart from fortune,] your, equal
in world, will not be there

verses.devanagari:
एतद्विद्याद्वये लब्धे न भवेत्सदृशस्तव |
बला चातिबला चैव सर्वज्ञानस्य मातरौ
verses.iast:
etat vidyā dvaye labdhe na bhavet sadṛśaḥ tava |
balā ca atibalā caiva sarva GYānasya mātarau
verses.translation: "On receiving these two teachings there will be none similar to you, for bala and atibala are the mothers of all knowledge.

glosses.meaning: these, teachings, two of them, on receiving
your, similar, will not, be there
by bala and atibala, also, only

verses.devanagari:
क्षुत्पिपासे न ते राम भविष्येते नरोत्तम |
बलामतिबलां चैव पठतस्तात राघव
verses.iast:
kṣut pipāse na te rāma bhaviṣyete narottama |
balām atibalām caiva paṭhataḥ tāta rāghava
verses.translation: "Oh, best one among men, Raghava, if you go on reciting bala and atiblala hymns, my dear Rama, there will be no hunger or thirst to you.

verses.devanagari:
गृहाण सर्वलोकस्य गुप्तये रघुनन्दन |
विद्याद्वयमधीयाने यशश्चाप्यतुलं भुवि |
पितामहसुते ह्येते विद्ये तेजःसमन्विते
प्रदातुं तव काकुत्स्थ सदृशस्त्वं हि धार्मिक |
verses.iast:
gṛhāṇa sarva lokasya guptaye raghu nandana |
vidyā dvayam adhīyāne yaśaḥ ca atha bhavet bhuvi |
pitāmaha sute hi ete vidye tejaḥ samanvite
pradātum tava kākutthsa sadṛaśaḥ tvam hi pārthiva |
verses.translation: "And if these twin teachings are practised an inestimable renown will also accrue, oh, Raghu's legatee, these two hymns that possess brilliance are the daughters of Forefather Brahma, and oh, Rama of Kakutstha, I intend to impart these hymns to you, oh virtuous one, as you are the most eligible one, hence take the teachings that are kept safe from the world.

glosses.meaning: hi you are, befitting - most eligible one, indeed
from all, world, kept safe, [are these teachings.]

verses.devanagari:
कामं बहुगुणाः सर्वे त्वय्येते नात्र संशयः |
तपसा संभृते चैते बहुरूपे भविष्यतः |
verses.iast:
kāmam bahuguṇāḥ sarve tvayi ete na atra saṃśayaḥ |
tapasā sambhṛte ca ete bahu rūpe bhaviṣyataḥ |
verses.translation: "Though all of these numerous qualities are undoubtedly available with you, that too in abundance, yet these hymns if ascetically nurtured will yield various results." Thus spoke Sage Vishvamitra to Rama.

glosses.meaning: the become - yield various kinds of results.

verses.devanagari:
ततो रामो जलं स्पृष्ट्वा प्रहृष्टवदनः शुचिः |
प्रतिजग्राह ते विद्ये महर्षेर्भावितात्मनः |
verses.iast:
tato rāmo jalam spṛṣṭvā prahṛṣṭa vadanaḥ śuciḥ |
prati jagrāha te vidye maharṣer bhāvita ātmanaḥ |
verses.translation: Then Rama on touching water to purify himself received those teachings from the contemplative soul Vishvamitra with gladness beaming on his face.

verses.devanagari:
विद्यासमुदितो रामः शुशुभे भूरिविक्रमः
सहस्ररश्मिर्भगवान् शरदीव दिवाकरः |
गुरुकार्याणि सर्वाणि नियुज्य कुशिकात्मजे |
ऊषुस्तां रजनीं तत्र सरय्वाः सुसुखं त्रयः
verses.iast:
vidyā samudito rāmaḥ śuśubhe bhīma vikramaḥ
sahasra raśmiḥ bhagvān śaradīva divākaraḥ |
guru kāryāṇi sarvāṇi niyujya kuśika ātmaje |
ūṣuḥ tām rajanīm tatra sarayvām susukham trayaḥ
verses.translation: Rama, the one with marvellous valiance, on obtaining those teachings performed all his duties of a student in respect of a teacher and then shone forth like the thousand rayed sun on a cloudless sky of autumn. Then those three very happily stayed on the riverbank of Sarayu for that night.
notes: Here guru kāryāṇi , are the duties demanded of a true disciple towards a guru, who is his mantra ācārya, teacher according hymns. Without performing these duties the studentship remains unfulfilled. These works are fetching food for teacher, arranging his bed, pressing his sore-legs called pāda samvāhana , etc. Rama does these services to any elderly person, more so to his father as at this canto 1-18-28.

Throughout this chapter Vishvamitra addresses Rama alone to learn the hymns. It may not be construed that Lakshmana is eliminated or avoided but he said to be one with Rama when it comes to education. Thus these hymn are imparted to Lakshmana also, not to Rama alone.

glosses.meaning: all, teacher's, works - works to be done in respect of teacher
sun, like - like sun with thousands of sunbeams

verses.devanagari:
दशरथनृपसूनुसत्तमाभ्यां
तृणशयनेऽनुचिते सहोषिताभ्याम् |
कुशिकसुतवचोऽनुलालिताभ्यां |
सुखमिव सा विबभौ विभावरी च
verses.iast:
daśaratha nṛipa sūnu sattamābhyām
tṛṇa śayane anucite tadā uṣitābhyām |
kuśika suta vaco'nulālitābhyām |
sukhamiva sā vibabhau vibhāvarI ca
verses.translation: Though both Rama and Lakshmana slept on an undeserving grass bed, nestled by the comfortable words of Vishvamitra that night is as though pleasant to the noteworthy children of Dasharatha.

glosses.meaning: Dasharatha's, children, noteworthy ones - to Rama, Lakshmana
